title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck is working on the profinite fundamental group of the stacky quotient of U_{0,3} = P^1 - {0,1,inf} by S_3, which is essentially the moduli stack M_{1,1}. Two groups appear throughout:
- Gamma_Q, the absolute Galois group Gal(Qbar/Q).
- Gamma~_Q, a 'Teichmüller-ized' version of it. It plays the role of a GT-hat-type group (GT-hat: profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group) acting on these fundamental groups.

The groups M_0^!, M_{0,3}^{!~}, M_{0,3}^~ and M_1 are extensions of Gamma~_Q by geometric profinite groups:
- M_0^! ≅ M_{0,3}^{!~} is the extension corresponding (up to ~) to pi_1(U_{0,3,Q}).
- M_{0,3}^~ corresponds to pi_1 of M'_{1,1}, the moduli of elliptic curves mod ±1 (the rigidified stack).
- M_1 corresponds to M_{1,1} itself.

On the previous pages he studied 'sections' (splittings) of these extensions labelled b), c), which give extensions gamma_{rho,sigma}. He also studied characters epsilon_2, epsilon_3 with values in mu_2.

Step 1 (top of page). He proposes a further partial section defined over the index-2 subgroup Gamma'''~_Q = {x in Pi~_Q | epsilon_2(x) epsilon_3(x) = 1}. Read epsilon_2 as the character of Q(i) and epsilon_3 as that of Q(sqrt(-3)). Their product is then the character of Q(i·sqrt(-3)) = Q(sqrt 3). Hence his tentative notation M(sqrt 3), 'its generators f converging in Q(sqrt 3)'. He also floats M(j), with j a primitive cube root of unity.

Step 2 (self-correction). He stops himself ('je suis en train de déconner') and returns to the geometric meaning, which is Grothendieck's anabelian section dictionary. Sections of pi_1(U_{0,3,Q}) -> Gamma_Q correspond (up to ~) to:
- rational points of U_{0,3,Q};
- tangential base points over Q at the cusps (his 'v.b./Q').
Partial sections, defined over open subgroups, correspond to closed points, i.e. points with values in finite extensions of Q.

Step 3 (the dictionary applied).
- Section b) corresponds to the point 1/2. This is a fixed point of an involution of S_3 (lambda in {-1, 2, 1/2}), i.e. j-invariant 1728.
- The partial section of c) corresponds to the point -j. This is a primitive 6th root of unity, a root of z^2 - z + 1 = 0 and a fixed point of the order-3 automorphism z -> 1/(1-z), i.e. j-invariant 0.
- -j is a point of U_{0,3} over Q(cube root of 1). So the notation M(-j) is 'reasonable'.

Step 4 (lifting). The extension N_rho~ does not sit inside M_0^!. After dividing by mu one gets a section of M_{0,3}^~ over Gamma~_Q. As the next page explains, this is a 'curve mod symmetry' with j = 0 over Q.

Step 5 (next page, the apparent paradox). He suspects this section does not lift to M_1 over all of Gamma~_Q, because the extension N_rho of Gamma~_Q by mu is non-trivial. He then worries this would mean no elliptic curve over Q has j = 0, which he himself calls absurd.

Overall purpose. To anchor the combinatorial/algebraic sections of the 'équation des lacets' (GT-type relations of order 2 and 3) to the S_3-orbifold points 1/2 and -j. These are the elliptic points of M_{1,1}, and he wants to understand the Galois/GT action at them.
errors: The tentative attachment of the partial section over ker(epsilon_2 epsilon_3) to a 'point' M(sqrt 3) or M(j) is withdrawn by Grothendieck himself ('déconner'). Under his own dictionary, the field of definition of the orbifold point -j is Q(sqrt -3), not Q(sqrt 3). The kernel of epsilon_2 epsilon_3 corresponds to Q(sqrt 3), whose relation to any special point is unclear.

Gap carried onto the next page. The worry that non-liftability of the section M_{0,3}^~ -> M_1 would imply no elliptic curve over Q with j = 0 is unfounded. y^2 = x^3 + 1 exists over Q.
- The mu_2-gerbe M_{1,1} -> M'_{1,1} is neutral at field-valued points. A 'curve mod ±1' is P^1 with a rational marked point and a degree-4 branch divisor, so a double cover y^2 = cubic always exists.
- Any obstruction must therefore come from the chosen section. Sections attached to a stacky point with mu_3/mu_6 automorphisms are only defined up to twisting by H^1. Alternatively it comes from working over Gamma~_Q (the GT-type group) rather than Gamma_Q.
- Grothendieck does not resolve this on these pages.

ideas.what: Sections of pi_1(U_{0,3,Q}) -> Gal(Qbar/Q) correspond to rational points and tangential base points; partial sections correspond to closed points over finite extensions
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983), published in Geometric Galois Actions I (1997); Esquisse d'un programme (anabelian ideas)

ideas.what: Identifying the special points 1/2 (order-2 fixed point, j = 1728) and -j (primitive 6th root of unity, order-3 fixed point, j = 0) of P^1-{0,1,inf} with sections of the extensions underlying the order-2 and order-3 relations
ideas.modern_name: Elliptic (orbifold) points of M_{1,1}; torsion in pi_1 of M_{1,1}/M_{0,4} and GT/Galois action on it
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps for the 2- and 3-cycle relations; Collas, Collas–Maugeais for Galois/GT action on torsion and special loci
ideas.where_published: Only implicitly in Esquisse (the 'two-level' Teichmüller tower, special points); explicit treatment here unpublished

ideas.what: Character bookkeeping: epsilon_2 (Q(i)) times epsilon_3 (Q(sqrt -3)) gives the character of Q(sqrt 3), defining an index-2 subgroup of Gamma~_Q
ideas.modern_name: Quadratic characters of the Galois/GT group

ideas.what: Lifting sections from pi_1 of the rigidified stack M'_{1,1} (curves mod ±1) to pi_1 of M_{1,1} through the mu_2-gerbe, with the obstruction measured by an extension of Gamma~_Q by mu
ideas.modern_name: Rigidification of stacks / gerbe obstruction; section conjecture for stacks (M_{1,1})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Abramovich–Corti–Vistoli (rigidification); stacky section conjecture studied later, e.g. Bresciani (unsure)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets out to compare liftability of a section of pi_1(M'_{1,1}) to pi_1(M_{1,1}) over the GT-type group Gamma~_Q with liftability over Gal(Q). He suspects the extension N_rho of Gamma~_Q by mu is non-trivial and so blocks the lift. Over Gal(Q) the lift must exist, since rational j = 0 curves exist. A genuine non-liftability over Gamma~_Q would therefore be an arithmetic invariant distinguishing GT-hat-type groups from Gal(Qbar/Q), located at the j = 0 orbifold point. The thread is left unresolved.
missed.quote: la section partielle M(-j) ici dans c) correspond au point -j de U_{0,3Q}, qui est dans U_{0,3}(Q[∛1]), donc la notation M(-j) raisonnable
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Whether GT-hat equals Gal(Qbar/Q) remains open. Obstructions at elliptic points (torsion of mapping class groups) are an active topic (Collas, Collas–Maugeais), and a mu_2-gerbe obstruction at j = 0 would be a concrete test case. Most likely, though, the non-liftability is an artifact of choosing the wrong twist of the section.

deep.surprise_reason: This is mostly exploratory and self-corrected ('déconner'). The section dictionary and the identification of 1/2 and -j with the order-2 and order-3 S_3 fixed points are known in the GT/anabelian literature. The only faint novelty is the unresolved gerbe-lifting question over the GT-type group, and it probably rests on a confusion.
transcription_corrections: Line 'Mo^! -> Gamma_Q^~ ≃ gamma_{rho,r}': the subscript is probably gamma_{rho,sigma}, consistent with the previous page.
'points v.b./Q' is an insertion above the crossed-out 'de'. It probably abbreviates the base-point notion (tangential base points / 'voisinages de base'); the reading is uncertain.
'points de U_{0,3Q} : valeurs des deux coordonnées ... fermés de Q' more plausibly reads 'points de U_{0,3Q} à valeurs dans des extensions finies de Q' (points fermés).
'Comment : N_rho~, elle n'est ... ⊂ M_0^!' is probably 'Comme pour N_rho~, elle n'est pas ⊂ M_0^! – mais en la divisant par mu ; on trouve après division par mu une section'.
The margin note ('? Mérite une ca. ann. Ntif.') is underlined and largely illegible. It may be a self-critical remark (e.g. 'Mérite ...'); the transcription is unreliable.
'M(sqrt 3) [-avec-] [?] plus encore M(j)' probably reads 'M(sqrt 3) ou plus encore M(j)' or similar.
